Contributing to onepagr

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for taking an interest in onepagr. This page explains how to report a problem, how to set up for development, and the conventions the project follows, so that a change is easy to review.

Reporting a problem or asking for a feature

Please open an issue at https://github.com/andrew-farrey/onepagr/issues. A useful bug report has:

  • a minimal example that reproduces it, ideally using example_data() so nobody needs your data,
  • the output of onepagr::check_quarto() and sessionInfo(),
  • what you expected and what happened instead.

For an accessibility problem, attach the PDF and say which checker or screen reader reported it. A problem that passes the automated checkers but fails a person is exactly what we want to hear about.

Setting up

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::load_all()
devtools::test()
devtools::check()

Rendering needs Quarto 1.10 or newer, which bundles Typst 0.15.1 or newer. Tests that need it skip themselves when it is missing; run onepagr::check_quarto() to see what you have.

Code, tests and documentation

  • Style. The tidyverse style guide, enforced by the lintr settings in .lintr (lines up to 100 characters). lintr::lint_package() should report nothing. Please do not reformat code you are not otherwise changing.
  • Documentation. roxygen2 with markdown. Edit the roxygen comments, then run devtools::document(). Write plainly, in short sentences.
  • Tests. testthat 3rd edition, one behavior per test, named for the behavior. A test that needs Quarto starts with skip_if_not(quarto::quarto_available()). Tests must never call install_quarto() or anything else that downloads software. For a bug fix, write the failing test first.
  • Dependencies. Call optional packages as pkg::fn() behind a requireNamespace() guard, and declare what you use in DESCRIPTION.

Changing a template, component, theme or asset

onepagr exists to produce accessible PDFs, so these changes carry extra checks. Before opening a pull request:

  1. Render all 15 template and theme combinations from example_data() (Rscript data-raw/gallery-images.R renders the gallery set).
  2. Check each PDF with veraPDF (--flavour ua1) and pdfa11y.
  3. Measure text contrast against the lightest end of every gradient it sits on. A color that passes where the text happens to sit can still fail at the other end of the gradient.
  4. Run PAC by hand on the changed templates. PAC is a manual check, and its AI-assisted tab is advisory. The README lists the findings already reviewed.
  5. Regenerate the gallery images if anything looks different.

Say in the pull request what you ran and what it showed.

Branches, commits and pull requests

  • Branch names are a short kebab-case topic, such as type-spacing or tokenize-headings. No version numbers or prefixes.
  • Commit messages start with an imperative, sentence-case subject of about 70 characters or fewer and no trailing period (“Add example_data() and template_data() starter-list helpers”). Use the body to explain why. One logical change per commit. No feat: or fix: prefixes.
  • Pull request titles follow the same style. The body uses the sections in the pull request template: Summary, Why, Behavior to know about, and Verification.
  • Keep a pull request to one topic. Include the tests, the documentation and the NEWS.md entry in the same pull request.

NEWS

Add an entry under # onepagr (development version) in NEWS.md for anything a user would notice. Write each bullet as a complete sentence about what changed for the reader, in the present tense, and lead with the function or topic in backticks when one function is the subject. Group entries under ## headings only when there are many. If your change comes from an issue or a pull request, end the bullet with (#123), and thank outside contributors with (@username).

Code of conduct

Please note that onepagr is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By contributing you agree to abide by its terms (see CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
